articles.title: Xuxa revela que primeiro neto será menino no Domingão com Huck | G1
articles.standfirst: Apresentadora contou o sexo do bebê durante participação da filha e do genro no programa deste domingo (22). Sasha está no quinto mês de gestação.
articles.summary: Xuxa revelou que o bebê de Sasha Meneghel e João Lucas é um menino durante o Domingão com Huck, relembrando quando anunciou a própria gravidez no palco do programa.
articles.body:
Xuxa revela sexo do neto no 'Caldeirão do Hulk'. — Foto: Reprodução / TV Globo

Xuxa revelou neste domingo (22) que seu primeiro neto, filho de Sasha Meneghel e João Lucas, é um menino. A apresentadora contou o sexo do bebê durante a participação do casal no " Domingão com Huck ".

A revelação aconteceu depois de Luciano Huck conversar com Sasha e João Lucas sobre a gestação e chamar Xuxa para participar do programa por vídeo.

Ao lembrar que Xuxa tem fama de não conseguir guardar segredos, o genro provocou a apresentadora sobre o sexo do bebê.

"Conta o sexo do bebê, então, pra gente", pediu João.

Sasha e João Lucas confirmaram a informação. O casal disse ainda que o bebê não tem nome definido.

A participação teve um simbolismo especial para a família. O programa relembrou que foi naquele palco, na época apresentado por Faustão, que Xuxa anunciou que estava grávida de Sasha.

Durante a atração deste domingo, foram exibidas imagens daquele momento e também do nascimento de Sasha. Xuxa contou que havia prometido a Faustão que revelaria a gravidez no programa assim que soubesse.

"Eu soube no sábado, no domingo eu estava [no programa]", afirmou.

Sasha e João Lucas no palco do Caldeirão do Hulk. — Foto: Reprodução//TV Globo

Sasha também contou que está com cerca de cinco meses de gestação e disse que sempre teve o desejo de ser mãe jovem.

"São muitas mudanças. Eu acho que uma mulher começa a sentir a gravidez muito antes do bebê chegar, que de fato vai mudar a nossa vida. Acho que a minha vida já começou a mudar."

Ela também afirmou que segue trabalhando e que tem recebido apoio de João Lucas e de sua equipe.

"Estou muito feliz. Sempre foi um sonho ser mãe. Eu sempre sonhei em ser mãe jovem e estou feliz de estar vivendo isso."

João Lucas falou sobre as mudanças na rotina do casal desde a descoberta da gravidez.

"Eu não tenho um bebê aqui no meu colo ainda, mas a vida muda, o centro da vida muda. A gente sai do centro", disse.

Xuxa conta reação ao saber que seria avó

Xuxa ao contar sexo do primeiro neto. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Xuxa também relembrou como recebeu a notícia da gravidez da filha. Segundo a apresentadora, sua primeira reação foi de euforia.

"Eu achei que eu ia gritar, que ia desmaiar. Eu saí correndo pela casa, xingando. Cada um tem uma reação. A minha foi só falar palavrão. Eu gritei muito."

Ela contou ainda que desejava ser avó havia muitos anos. Segundo Xuxa, a vontade surgiu quando viu a própria mãe segurando Sasha no colo ainda bebê.

"Assim que eu vi a minha mãe segurando a Sasha no colo, na chegada em casa, eu falei: 'Quero ser avó'."

articles.title: VÍDEO: Novas imagens mostram destruição após supercélula no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeito estima que 8 mil casas foram atingidas. Defesa Civil aponta indícios de microexplosão com ventos de 114 km/h na cidade gaúcha. Cinco pessoas morreram.
articles.summary: Prefeito estima que 8 mil casas foram atingidas. Defesa Civil aponta indícios de microexplosão com ventos de 114 km/h na cidade gaúcha. Cinco pessoas morreram.
articles.body:
Novas imagens mostram como ficou o município de Tupanciretã , na Região Central do Rio Grande do Sul, após a passagem de uma supercélula com indícios microexplosão e ventos de 114 km/h na madrugada de sexta-feira (20). Cinco pessoas morreram .

Vídeos e fotos aéreos foram captados por Guto Drones e cedidos ao g1 . Todos os comércios do centro da cidade foram atingidos. Uma empresa estima prejuízo milionário após ter unidades afetadas. O número oficial de casas atingidas é de 5 mil, segundo a Defesa Civil gaúcha, enquanto a prefeitura estima que mais de 8 mil residências tenham tido algum tipo de dano . (Veja no vídeo acima)

O Centro de Monitoramento da Defesa Civil do RS analisou imagens e vídeos da tempestade e afirma que há indícios de que a cidade tenha sido atingida por uma microexplosão . Uma estação do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) registrou rajadas de vento de 114 km/h durante o temporal.

"Até o momento, não é possível confirmar a ocorrência de um tornado no município. As evidências apontam para ventos severos associados à supercélula, possivelmente provocados por uma microexplosão. A possibilidade de tornado não está completamente descartada, mas o fenômeno, isoladamente, não explicaria a extensão dos danos registrados na cidade", destaca a Defesa Civil.

🔎 O que é supercélula: de acordo com a Climatempo Meteorologia, é "uma tempestade muito organizada, marcada por uma corrente de ar ascendente que permanece ativa e gira".

articles.title: Não foi tornado: meteorologistas explicam 'supercélula' e microexplosão que devastaram cidade no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Temporal deixou 265 feridos e destruiu silos agrícolas e casas; árvores tombadas na mesma direção indicam corrente de ar descendente.
articles.summary: Temporal deixou 265 feridos e destruiu silos agrícolas e casas; árvores tombadas na mesma direção indicam corrente de ar descendente.
articles.body:
Uma tempestade severa com granizo e ventos que podem ter superado os 200 quilômetros por hora atingiu Tupanciretã, no centro do Rio Grande do Sul, na madrugada de sexta-feira (20), deixando cinco mortos, 265 feridos e 48 desabrigados, segundo a Defesa Civil. Embora muitos moradores tenham associado a destruição a um tornado, meteorologistas apontam que o município de pouco mais de 20 mil habitantes foi atingido por uma supercélula acompanhada de microexplosões.

O temporal destelhou quase toda a cidade, retorceu vigas metálicas e deixou esqueletos de concreto expostos. Na zona produtiva, silos de aço galvanizado de quase 30 metros de altura e 30 toneladas usados para armazenar sementes de soja foram torcidos, arremessando chapas de metal a metros de distância. A chuva também danificou laboratórios, armazéns e 60 mil sacas de sementes prontas para comercialização.

"Certamente a tempestade que atingiu o Rio Grande do Sul naquele dia ela foi uma supercélula", afirma o pós-doutorando em Meteorologia da Universidade Federal de Santa Maria (UFSM), Maurício Oliveira. Trata-se de uma das tempestades mais severas da natureza, alimentada por uma corrente ascendente de ar quente e úmido que sobe girando a velocidades que podem superar 200 km/h e sustenta pedras de granizo no alto até ganharem peso.

"Essa corrente ascendente é mais intensa. Então ela consegue manter, por exemplo, o granizo por mais tempo dentro da nuvem, essas pedras podem ser maiores ou até mesmo em maior quantidade", explica o doutor em Meteorologia da UFSM, Murilo Lopes.

Quando a nuvem não suporta o peso do gelo e da chuva, o material despenca e arrasta o ar frio e denso em direção ao solo num fenômeno chamado downburst (corrente descendente). "Esse ar mais frio ele é mais denso e, em algumas situações, como aconteceu em Tupanciretã, esse movimento de ar é muito intenso, né, e ao chegar no solo ele se espalha lateralmente provocando fortes rajadas de vento", detalha Lopes.

A diferença entre um tornado e uma corrente descendente é identificada pelas marcas deixadas no solo. "O tornado ele funciona como uma espécie de aspirador de pó, então as coisas vão em direção a ele, e a microexplosão ela tem esse movimento de espalhamento lateral, e aí isso acaba provocando muitas vezes a queda de árvores numa direção só", explica Murilo Lopes. Em Tupanciretã, bosques inteiros tiveram árvores quebradas ao meio e tombadas para o mesmo lado.

Especialistas estimam que os ventos tenham passado de 200 km/h em pontos isolados. Imagens do satélite Goes-19 registraram o avanço do sistema com topos de nuvens extremamente frios e altos sobre o centro do estado. "Essa em Tupanciretã é um dos casos mais intensos que eu já vi acontecer no Brasil", avalia Maurício Oliveira. Uma equipe da UFSM fará o mapeamento em campo da área devastada.

O Sul do Brasil possui características geográficas semelhantes às do "Corredor dos Tornados" nos Estados Unidos, pois a Cordilheira dos Andes desvia o ar quente e úmido da Amazônia para o sul, onde encontra fortes correntes de jato em altitude.

Segundo levantamento da rede Prevots, o país já soma mais de 22 mil relatos de tempo severo em 2026, mais que o dobro de todo o ano de 2025. Na mesma semana, dois tornados atingiram Foz do Iguaçu e Manoel Ribas, no Paraná. Outras tempestades também atingiram o estado, deixando mais de 350 mil imóveis sem luz no estado.

Apesar de a tecnologia atual permitir prever supercélulas, especialistas alertam para a carência de equipamentos de monitoramento. "Os radares meteorológicos são as ferramentas mais importantes pro acompanhamento da evolução dessas tempestades e identificar se aquela tempestade tem um potencial causador de granizo e até mesmo pra formação de tornados e de microexplosões. Atualmente no Rio Grande do Sul nós contamos com poucos radares ainda", observa Murilo Lopes.

No clube Rancho Country, onde ocorreria um baile na madrugada de sexta, os integrantes da Banda Legal sobreviveram ao desabamento do salão. "O primeiro passo é que a luz caiu. E aí começou o vento com chuva e granizo", relata o vocalista Joel Antes.

"Tinha uma porta, que era a porta principal do salão, que o vento arrastou. E quando arrastou a porta, levou toda a estrutura do teto. Do telhado. E caiu as quatro paredes do salão", lembra o também vocalista Alex Lopes.

Abrigados nos banheiros, os músicos viram uma das paredes ceder antes de correrem para o ônibus da equipe, que teve o vidro traseiro estourado pelo granizo.

Cristiano Gasperin, de Caxias do Sul, filmou o temporal da casa dos sogros após acordar às 3h com o estrondo no telhado e levar a família para o andar inferior. "Tinha cerca de meio metro de pedra em toda a rua", conta. A torre da igreja vizinha desabou sobre o carro dele, enquanto as pedras de gelo perfuraram o forro da residência.

Entre as cinco vítimas fatais está dona Hortênsia, cuja casa foi completamente destruída. A neta, a assistente administrativa Ethyene Alves, havia deixado a cidade à meia-noite e recebeu uma ligação do filho às 3h30 alertando sobre o temporal.

"E aí, a tia botou no grupo da família pedindo socorro pela vó. E aí nisso, os telefones começaram a sinal cair. Não tinha luz. Aí no que clareou, meu filho conseguiu atravessar a cidade a pé. Ele ainda conseguiu ver a vó em vida. Estava bem abalado. Ele conseguiu, ele pegou a mão dela. Disse que ela apertava a mão dele", conta Ethyene. Dona Hortênsia morreu a caminho do hospital de uma cidade vizinha.

O filho dela, o caminhoneiro Luís Bueno Alves, também teve a residência destruída nos fundos do terreno, mas participa do mutirão comunitário na cidade. "Todo mundo se ajudando. Estamos tentando ajudar outras pessoas também. Agora, graças a Deus, tá tudo mais alinhado. Vamos superar", afirma.

articles.title: Carlos Nobre revela diagnóstico de ELA e diz que seguirá trabalhando pela Amazônia aos 75 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Cientista brasileiro conta como descobriu esclerose lateral amiotrófica após a COP30 e detalha projetos como fábricas de chocolate indígenas e instituto pan-amazônico.
articles.summary: Cientista brasileiro conta como descobriu esclerose lateral amiotrófica após a COP30 e detalha projetos como fábricas de chocolate indígenas e instituto pan-amazônico.
articles.body:
O climatologista brasileiro Carlos Nobre, de 75 anos, foi diagnosticado com esclerose lateral amiotrófica (ELA), uma doença neurodegenerativa grave e sem cura. A descoberta afastou pela primeira vez em 31 anos um dos cientistas mais respeitados do mundo de uma edição da Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre as Mudanças Climáticas (COP).

Em entrevista ao Fantástico, Nobre falou sobre a rotina após o diagnóstico e reafirmou que não pretende interromper as pesquisas nem a defesa da Amazônia. "Lá no tempo do meu pai, do meu avô, eles na minha idade, todo mundo aposentado. Eu tenho 75 anos. Mas agora nós chegamos num ponto que o risco do planeta é tão grande, que a gente sempre procura continuar trabalhando. Eu continuo trabalhando", afirma o pesquisador.

A ausência do brasileiro na COP31 chamou a atenção da comunidade científica internacional e foi explicada durante o evento pelo presidente do BNDES, Aloizio Mercadante. "Eu quero aqui fazer uma homenagem a um cientista. Participou de todas as COPs, hoje ele não tá aqui. Não tá aqui porque ele tá com ELA, que é a esclerose lateral amiotrófica. Que é o Carlos Nobre, meu amigo, uma grande salva de palmas para ele", declarou Mercadante.

Mesmo acompanhando as discussões à distância, o climatologista avaliou as metas climáticas debatidas. "Essa é uma meta da COP31. Mas isso é muito pouco", comentou sobre a projeção de atingir 35% de eletricidade renovável até 2035.

A ELA atinge os neurônios motores responsáveis por enviar comandos do cérebro aos músculos. Segundo o neurologista Mário Jorge, a condição provoca perda progressiva da mobilidade sem causar dor ou alterações sensitivas, podendo evoluir para comprometimento respiratório. Estudos indicam que apenas 10% dos casos têm origem genética, enquanto 90% ocorrem de forma esporádica.

Os primeiros sintomas surgiram em dezembro de 2025, dias após a COP30, em Belém. "Ele começou a ter dificuldade motora com o braço direito, além de perder a força, ele foi notando também um certo grau de atrofia na mão e inchaço também", relata o médico, detalhando que o diagnóstico foi confirmado por meio de eletroneuromiografia. Para o neurologista, a postura ativa do paciente favorece a continuidade da produção intelectual. "Eu vejo isso com muito otimismo, porque ele não se entregou. Ele tá lutando contra a doença. Como ele tem uma reserva cognitiva muito grande, ele vai poder ainda produzir muita coisa", avalia.

Trajetória científica e alerta sobre o ponto de não retorno

Único brasileiro membro da The Royal Society, a academia nacional de ciências do Reino Unido, Nobre também integra as academias de ciências do Brasil e dos Estados Unidos. Após concluir o doutorado no Instituto de Tecnologia de Massachusetts (MIT), em 1983, recusou propostas acadêmicas nos EUA para retornar ao país.

"Eu recebi três ofertas de trabalho lá, duas ofertas de pós-doutorado e uma oferta de professor assistente de uma universidade. E eu tomei a melhor decisão da minha vida. Eu falei não. Eu volto para o Brasil. Porque quando eu era bem jovem, 20, 21 anos, foi quando eu conheci a Amazônia, eu me apaixonei pela Amazônia", relembra.

Durante mais de três décadas no Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe), em São José dos Campos (SP), liderou estudos climáticos e idealizou o Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden).

O cientista ficou conhecido mundialmente por alertar sobre o risco de "savanização" caso o desmatamento ultrapasse de 20% a 25% da floresta. Embora dados do Inpe mostrem uma queda de 67% na derrubada desde 2019 — atingindo em 2026 o menor índice da série histórica iniciada em 1988 —, Nobre alerta para o impacto combinado com o aquecimento global.

Projetos para a bioeconomia e recado às novas gerações

Além de apontar os riscos, o pesquisador passou a estruturar alternativas econômicas para manter a floresta em pé por meio do projeto Amazônia 4.0, que instala biofábricas em comunidades tradicionais. "Estamos agora concluindo a primeira fábrica numa comunidade indígena, fábrica de chocolate. Eles vão produzir 100 a 150 quilos de chocolate por dia", destaca.

Outro plano em andamento aos 75 anos é a criação do Amazônia Instituto de Tecnologia (Amit), instituição pan-amazônica com seis polos de inovação voltados exclusivamente para formação e pesquisa sobre a preservação do bioma. "Nosso plano é, em dois anos, construir toda a infraestrutura educacional, todos os polos de inovação e aí começar", projeta.

Ao avaliar o cenário climático global, Nobre deixa um apelo aos mais jovens. "O que eu falo para as novas gerações é: não façam o que a minha geração. Não estão combatendo essa gigantesca emergência climática", conclui.

articles.title: Defesa Civil de Niterói: Alerta de inundação adia show de Gil | G1
articles.standfirst: O alerta foi recebido por moradores em seus celulares. Apresentação acontecerá 20 de dezembro.
articles.summary: Após alerta severo da Defesa Civil de Niterói para riscos de alagamentos, o show de Gilberto Gil foi remarcado para 20 de dezembro por segurança.
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil de Niterói emitiu um alerta severo de risco de alagamentos e inundações neste domingo (22). O alerta foi recebido por moradores em seus celulares.

Em virtude do tempo, o show de Gilberto Gil em comemoração ao aniversário da cidade foi adiado para o dia 20 de dezembro, como informou a prefeitura e o próprio artista em suas redes sociais.

"Em função das condições climáticas e do avanço de uma formação de nuvens de chuva e raios identificada na região da Ilha do Governador, em direção à Niterói, o show de Gilberto Gil em comemoração ao aniversário de Niterói foi adiado para o próximo dia 20 de dezembro. A Defesa Civil de Niterói acompanha continuamente a evolução das condições do tempo, por meio de seus sistemas de monitoramento, para garantir a segurança e o bem-estar da população e informa que a chuva pode não ser tão intensa, mas com possibilidade de muitos raios", disse a Prefeitura de Niterói, em nota.

articles.title: 'Uma vergonha': Líderes europeus criticam teor do texto final da COP31 | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao deixar a plenária da conferência, representantes europeus acusaram empresas petrolíferas de sequestrar o texto final da COP31. Resolução não se compromete com o fim do uso dos combustíveis fósseis.
articles.summary: Representantes da União Europeia protestam contra a falta de ambição na COP31 e denunciam a influência de petroleiras no texto final sobre combustíveis fósseis.
articles.body:
Líderes e delegados da União Europeia abandonam a plenária da COP31 após rejeitarem acordo final sobre combustíveis fósseis na manhã deste domingo (20) , em Antália, na Turquia .

O movimento, visto como forma de protesto, antecedeu o fim da conferência, que confirmou a falta de consenso.

Conversando com jornalistas do lado de fora da plenária, os representantes do UE explicaram que a proposta apresentada pela presidência da conferência falhou em colocar a ciência como pilar central das negociações e em assegurar uma transição energética justa.

Segundo o comissário da União Europeia para o Clima , Wopke Hoestra, o texto tentou desviar o foco da redução efetiva de petróleo, gás e carvão ao apostar de forma desproporcional na captura e armazenamento de carbono (CCS, na sigla em inglês).

"A captura de carbono caiu do céu como a nova solução para tudo, como se pudéssemos esquecer os combustíveis fósseis e simplesmente usar essa tecnologia para sair do problema. Isso não é aceitável, e fazemos isso com o coração pesado junto a muitos outros países, mas simplesmente não podemos aceitar".

Apesar do rompimento com o texto final, os representantes disseram manter apoio ao multilateralismo, à solidariedade global e à continuidade do processo da COP, mesmo diante das fraturas expostas no encontro.

Turkey hosts UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya — Foto: Kaan Soyturk

Acusações de sabotagem por companhias de combustíveis fósseis

O ministro do Clima da Irlanda , Darragh O'Brien, relatou que todas as tentativas de incluir emendas consideradas básicas — como a simples menção aos combustíveis fósseis e à necessidade de transição energética — foram sistematicamente barradas pelas copresidências da conferência.

"O rascunho de decisão apresentado hoje na COP não dialoga com a realidade da crise climática que o nosso mundo enfrenta e não tem a ambição necessária", disse O'Brien, ponderando que houve bons avanços paralelos em áreas como eletrificação e resíduo zero, mas lamentando o desfecho do documento principal.

O ministro irlandês acusou o texto de ter sido cooptado por interesses do setor petrolífero: "Não poderíamos, em sã consciência, apoiar um texto que efetivamente nega o que está acontecendo no mundo e que foi sequestrado pelos produtores de combustíveis fósseis".

O'Brien revelou ainda que, antes da saída da plenária, as delegações tentaram negociar uma declaração factual curta, apenas para registrar que há países comprometidos com a trajetória de abandono dos combustíveis fósseis. A iniciativa, contudo, também acabou vetada.

"Isso é uma vergonha e não vamos tolerar", criticou o ministro. "Nossos cidadãos, nossos vizinhos e nossos irmãos e irmãs em toda a União Europeia e no mundo não nos agradeceriam por aceitar um texto que, em vários aspectos, é baseado em uma irrealidade."

A saída da delegação europeia e de outros negociadores esvaziou a plenária.

Turkey hosts COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya — Foto: Murad Sezer

Em conversas com jornalistas, o presidente turco da COP31, Murat Kurum, também reconheceu o impasse criado por um grupo de países que não se comprometeram com o fim do uso de combustíveis fósseis.

"Infelizmente, eles impediram o andamento do processo e não há mais nada a ser feito"

Recorde de duração e críticas a falta de 'ambiação'

A COP31 é a 31ª conferência do clima da ONU, encontro anual que reúne governos, cientistas, organizações ambientais e representantes da sociedade civil para discutir medidas de enfrentamento à crise climática.

A sigla COP significa “Conferência das Partes”, em referência aos países que integram a Convenção-Quadro das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima.

A conferência é realizada desde 1995, com exceção de 2020, por causa da pandemia.

Neste ano, o encontro acontece em Antália, no sul da Turquia. A primeira semana da cúpula foi marcada por reuniões técnicas e pela apresentação de propostas.

Na segunda, ministros e representantes de alto nível assumiram parte das negociações para tentar resolver os principais impasses.

Entre os temas centrais estão justamente a transição para longe dos combustíveis fósseis, o financiamento climático e a adaptação aos impactos do aquecimento global, como secas, enchentes e ondas de calor.

A COP31 tornou-se a conferência mais longa da história, depois de ultrapassar 44 horas de prorrogação após o final previsto. O encontro de Antália bateu o recorde da COP25 em Madri, em 2019.

O fracasso das negociações ocorre em um ano em que os impactos mais destrutivos do aquecimento global, como o calor extremo na Europa e as inundações glaciais no Nepal, foram ofuscados pelas demandas das guerras no Irã e na Ucrânia e pela indignação pública com o aumento vertiginoso do custo de vida.

Em 2025, após tomar posse em Washington, o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, determinou a retirada dos EUA do Acordo de Paris, documento que rege as COPs e que coordena as ações que os países devem tomar para combater as mudanças climáticas. Os EUA são um dos países mais poluidores do mundo.

O último grande impasse nas negociações climáticas da ONU ocorreu em Copenhague, em 2009, quando os países não conseguiram adotar o Acordo de Copenhague por consenso, representando um revés para a diplomacia climática multilateral.

A Austrália, que liderava as negociações, e a Turquia, país anfitrião, divulgaram várias versões de um texto que buscava um meio-termo entre as necessidades das nações mais vulneráveis ​​às mudanças climáticas e aquelas cujas economias dependem da produção ou do consumo de combustíveis fósseis.

Mas a tentativa de obter apoio consensual não teve sucesso, com os críticos do texto considerando-o pouco ambicioso.

articles.title: India, Nepal set to ink pacts on energy, infra, tech on Balen Shah's 1st visit
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Foreign minister S Jaishankar called on Nepal PM Balendra Shah, who arrived in India on Sunday for what is his first bilateral visit abroad.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Foreign minister S Jaishankar called on Nepal PM Balendra Shah, who arrived in India on Sunday for what is his first bilateral visit abroad. PM Modi will host Shah for their first in-person meeting on Monday that will be followed by an exchange of "forward-looking" agreements spanning key areas of cooperation: infrastructure, technology, connectivity, development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, climate change and disaster resilience."India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal. Look forward to his engagements with PM @narendramodi tomorrow," said Jaishankar in a post on X after the meeting. Official sources said that the leaders will virtually inaugurate several completed initiatives, apart from joining foundation stone-laying ceremonies for some new projects. Shah is also expected to reiterate Nepal's request for two-way low-altitude air entry corridors through Indian airspace near western border entry points.Securing direct air routes is essential for Nepal to attract international airlines and make its new Bhairahawa airport commercially viable. “This visit comes at an opportune moment when there is considerable synergy between the national priorities of both countries in terms of economic growth, social development, expansion of infrastructure, adoption of technology and addressing issues like natural disasters and climate change,” said a source, adding that the leaders will look to provide political direction that will shape the roadmap for bilateral cooperation for many years to come.The two sides have finalised a joint vision for bilateral relations that is expected to be released after the meeting. Nepal is also seeking an economic package worth $2 billion from India. While Shah may raise the boundary issue, it’s unlikely to be a sticking point in the meeting.India sees its ties with Nepal as unique and comprehensive, characterised by mutual trust, open borders, shared traditions and close people-to-people ties. Govt sources highlighted how India is Nepal’s largest trade, transit and investment partner. Nepal enjoys duty-free access to the Indian market and India is also Nepal’s biggest export destination and receives about 80% of Nepal’s goods exports, they said. The visit is expected to build upon the goodwill generated in Nepal by India’s assistance to the country after the devastating floods earlier this year. India provided about 140 tonnes of emergency supplies and extended technical assistance in tunnel rescue and forensic activities following the flash flood.India and Nepal are exploring the development of new pipelines and terminals to further enhance energy connectivity. articles.title: In 1898, Glasgow opened the People’s Palace as a museum for its citizens; 128 years later, a £10 million grant is backing restoration of its historic glasshouse ahead of a planned 2029 reopening
articles.summary: A common man always wonders what it would have felt like to be the Princes and Princesses who used to live in palaces.
articles.body: A common man always wonders what it would have felt like to be the Princes and Princesses who used to live in palaces. The scope of our imagination remains limited to the palaces that are open to visitors today which provide a glimpse of that life. In 1898, Glasgow opened the People’s Palace to give ordinary people a place to learn, explore, relax and enjoy themselves while experiencing the Palace. More than a century later, a £10 million grant will be supporting the restoration of its historic Winter Gardens glasshouse. The announcement, made on November 17, 2026 by the Heritage Fund, will help reopen the property for visitors.Where was the announcement madeThe project is aimed to be completed in two years with the planned reopening scheduled for December 2029. The restoration will include the museum and its glasshouse, including improving accessibility and making these historic buildings more environmentally sustainable. The project also includes a programme of community engagement to reimagine People’s Palace which remains as Glasgow’s much loved heritage site.A palace built for ordinary peopleThe People’s Palace is situated in Glasgow Green which is one of the oldest public parks in the United Kingdom. When it was opened in 1898, it was envisioned as a ‘palace of pleasure and imagination', a civic space where the city's working population could spend time discovering the world beyond their everyday lives.The museum is built with red sandstone, gradually becoming a fascinating record of the city's social history, documenting everyday life, changing neighbourhoods, working conditions, politics and popular culture. They tell stories of Glasgow’s diverse communities from 1750, till today. The museum, thus, became a part of the city's culture and its people which did not remain restricted to Kings and explorers.The historic glasshouse, with its expansive glazed structure and traditional architectural character, offered visitors an opportunity to step into a greener environment. Traditionally, Glasgow has been an industrial hub, which made the graden a refreshing space for industrial workers and their families to experience. However, the Winter Gardens have been closed since 2019, while the People’s Palace itself shut in April 2024 for major refurbishment. The latest funding is particularly significant because it will help restore the glasshouse and reconnect it with the museum, allowing visitors to experience the two spaces as part of one destination.The restoration plansThe £10 million award from the National Lottery Heritage Fund is part of a wider restoration programme expected to cost approximately £50.86 million. The revived landmark will not just change the outlook of the museum but renew it in character. It will now be a dynamic, community-led museum with events space as well.Extending beyond the city's history, the museum will now consist of themes of Politics and Protest, Culture and Nightlife, and Housing, Health, and Homelife. A dedicated learning space on the ground floor will provide opportunities for educational activities and community participation. The renewd space wil also include some of the iconic older pieces including paintings by Ken Currie, the original signage from the Barrowland Ballroom and the iconic Banana Boots associated with comedian Billy Connolly.Councillor Ricky Bell, Leader of Glasgow City Council told Glasgow Life how “Glasgow and the National Lottery Heritage Fund have worked together to restore and reimagine some of our city's most treasured cultural landmarks.” He expressed his gratitude for the latest funding that will, according to him, breathe new life into one of Glasgow’s most iconic civic spaces, creating a vibrant home for the stories, collections and communities that have shaped” Glasgow.Eilish McGuinness, Chief Executive at The National Lottery Heritage Fund expressed “The People’s Palace and Winter Gardens belong at the heart of Glasgow. This much-loved historic landmark will be reimagined for future generations and we are excited to support its transformation.”Thus, the restoration of the Palace property will once again become an integral part of the city's museum landscape. It will provide people a space for respite and joy along with an understanding of what the city stands for.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: An Illinois motorcyclist badly injured when a pickup drove through an intersection won a $27.5 million jury verdict; an appeals court cut $10 million from damages and gave him a choice to accept or seek a new trial
articles.summary: An Illinois motorcyclist who was badly injured when a pickup drove through an intersection won a $27.5 million jury verdict.
articles.body: An Illinois motorcyclist who was badly injured when a pickup drove through an intersection won a $27.5 million jury verdict. The Fifth District Appellate Court has now cut $10 million from the damages award and given the rider a choice between accepting the reduced amount or seeking a new trial, according to the Illinois Courts’ recent opinions list and Justia U.S. Law.The case, Klucker v. Zobrist, was filed in the Fifth District Appellate Court and decided on November 19, 2026. The appellate court’s decision changes the financial outcome of the case but leaves the underlying liability finding intact.How the crash happenedThe motorcyclist was riding through an intersection when a pickup truck drove through the same intersection. The collision caused serious injuries and a large jury award. A motorcyclist filed suit for personal injury and the case went to trial. A jury found in his favour, and awarded him $27.5 million in damages. The size of the verdict was a reflection of the severity of the injuries and how the rider’s life had been impacted. The case then moved to the appellate court, where the damages figure was challenged.What the appeals court didThe appellate court reduced the damages award by $10 million. That brings the effective award down to $17.5 million, assuming the plaintiff accepts the reduced amount. The court gave the motorcyclist a choice. He can accept the reduced verdict or choose to seek a new trial on the damages issue. The decision does not erase the jury’s finding on liability. The issue is quantum of damages and whether the original award was supported by evidence.Why the court intervenedAppellate courts sometimes reduce damages when they find that a jury award is excessive or not supported by the record. In this case, the court found reason to reduce the amount by $10 million. The court’s decision gives the plaintiff a path forward. He can either take the reduced amount or ask for a new trial to revisit the damages calculation. The case is now part of the appellate court’s recent opinions list. It is listed as a Rule 23 decision, which means it is a nonprecedential opinion.What happens nextThe motorcyclist now has to decide whether to accept the reduced award or pursue a new trial. That decision will depend on how he and his legal team view the chances of getting a higher award in a second trial.If he accepts the reduced amount, the case can move toward final resolution. If he seeks a new trial, the damages issue will be reheard.The case shows how appellate review can change the outcome of a large personal injury verdict. It also highlights the importance of the trial record in determining whether a jury’s damages award will stand.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A missing letter on a 1964 Welsh map sparked a driveway row; after a glampsite owner tried to stop neighbours parking in their own garden, she lost, faced £135,000 in costs and is now appealing
articles.summary: A Welsh glamping site owner has been ordered to pay £135,000 in legal costs after a dispute over whether her neighbours can drive past their front door to
articles.body: A Welsh glamping site owner has been ordered to pay £135,000 in legal costs after a dispute over whether her neighbours can drive past their front door to reach their own parking space. Carol Esteban is now challenging the ruling at the Court of Appeal, according to AOL and The Independent.The case centres on a shared track at Cwmtawe Farm near Abercrave, close to the Brecon Beacons. Esteban argued that the neighbours’ right of way ended opposite their front door, while Neil and Nadine Gould said it extended far enough for them to park beside their home.How the dispute beganThe Goulds’ detached cottage, Cwmtawe Villa, is surrounded by land belonging to Cwmtawe Farm, where Esteban runs a glamping site across more than 60 acres. The properties were once held by the same owner, but the villa was sold off in 1949 and the original documents have been lost.A 1964 conveyancing document gave the villa’s owners an easement, allowing them to use the farm track on foot or by vehicle. The problem was that the map attached to that document was missing the letter B, which was meant to mark where the right of way ended. Esteban argued that the right of way stopped at the front door of the villa. The Goulds argued that it extended a few feet further, allowing them to turn into the hardstanding parking area beside their house.What the court decidedIn July 2025, Judge Milwyn Jarman ruled in favour of the Goulds. He found that their vehicular right of way extended to the space on the north side of the villa, where they currently park.The judge rejected Esteban’s argument that the right of way should stop at the front door. He said that interpretation would lead to impracticality, since the Goulds would be able to drive up to the door but not park or turn around. The court also ordered Esteban to pay £135,000 in legal costs. That figure has now become part of the appeal.Why the appeal mattersEsteban’s lawyers argue that the High Court judge did not properly interpret the 1949 conveyance. They say the judge instead decided what the parties should have agreed to, rather than what the documents actually said, as per the reports. They also argue that there is no evidence the track extended beyond the front door of Cwmtawe. The appeal focuses on whether the easement stops at the front door or allows the Goulds to reach their parking spaces.Esteban’s legal team also challenges the costs order. They point out that she succeeded on parts of her counterclaim, including a finding that a waterpipe had been installed unlawfully on her land.What the neighbours sayThe Goulds’ lawyers argue that the judge reached the right conclusion. They say the easement must allow the couple to reach their parking spaces, otherwise it would have little practical use.They argue that the layout of the land shows there is no physical feature stopping the Goulds from driving onto their parking area. The lawyers say the judge’s interpretation gives practical effect to what the original grantor intended.The appeal judges have reserved their decision. The outcome will determine whether the Goulds can continue using the track to access their parking space, and whether Esteban will have to pay the £135,000 costs bill.You use AI every day. articles.summary: iShowSpeed's excitement over GTA 6 quickly turned into frustration after a marathon gaming session ended with a result he never wanted.
articles.body: iShowSpeed's excitement over GTA 6 quickly turned into frustration after a marathon gaming session ended with a result he never wanted. The popular streamer spent more than two days completing Rockstar Games' latest release, only to discover that his choices had led to an ending he could not accept. Hoping to change the outcome, he tried to load an earlier save. Instead, one wrong move cost him a 98% completed game file. What should have been a second chance became another painful setback for the streamer.iShowSpeed spends 52 hours completing GTA 6 without sleepSpeed had originally promised his viewers that he would take a more relaxed approach to GTA 6. Before the launch, he planned to play for around 10 to 12 hours each day, giving himself and his audience enough time to enjoy the experience.However, his plans changed once the game became available.The streamer began playing on November 18 and continued until November 20, completing the main story in approximately 52 hours and 31 minutes. He pushed through the night and reportedly went without sleep for much of the three-day period.His marathon was not without technical problems. Around 43 hours into the session, his PlayStation 5 crashed during a cutscene. Speed feared that he had lost hours of progress, but the game's autosave feature helped him recover and continue.Eventually, he reached the final part of the story. However, the outcome left him visibly devastated. In his video titled "I BEAT GTA 6!", Speed repeatedly questioned what he had just witnessed before breaking down in front of his viewers.GTA 6 multiple endings cost iShowSpeed his 98% save fileThe biggest disappointment came when Speed decided to pursue a different ending. GTA 6 features several possible story outcomes, with player decisions influencing what happens to its central characters, Jason and Lucia.Unlike simply replaying a previous mission, changing the ending requires players to return to an earlier save. Speed attempted to do exactly that but selected the wrong file and accidentally overwrote his 98% completed save.The mistake meant he could no longer use that progress to explore another version of the ending. It was an especially frustrating outcome after spending more than 52 hours completing the story.GTA 6 also makes players think carefully about their decisions, as its story does not offer the same straightforward mission replay option found in earlier instalments.Speed's experience offers an important lesson for players eager to finish the game quickly. Creating separate save files before major story decisions can help protect progress and preserve the chance to explore different outcomes.After waiting more than a decade for Rockstar's latest Grand Theft Auto instalment, rushing through its story may not be the best way to experience everything it offers. Speed's marathon proved that sometimes slowing down is the smarter move.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: A father and daughter travelling to California for a family baptism were detained by masked US immigration officers at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, triggering a chaotic confrontation that was captured on video by fellow passengers.The two were boarding an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles on Saturday when Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained them on the jet bridge, AP reported. Videos circulating on social media showed officers struggling with someone on the ground, while the incident delayed the flight.The father and daughter, who have been living in the US since 2015 and are seeking asylum, have no criminal records, their lawyer Olia Catala told The Associated Press.“They’ve done everything correctly, and these are educated people,” Catala said, adding that the daughter had attended university and worked for a nonprofit organisation.ICE identified the father as Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who had overstayed his visa. The agency said another passenger, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, was also detained after allegedly throwing hot coffee at officers during the confrontation.However, Mejia's lawyer said she had married a US citizen and had filed paperwork to adjust her immigration status. Her husband, who was accompanying her and her father, was not detained.Both Mendoza and Mejia were being held at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, according to their lawyer.Alaska Airlines said ICE officers had not provided advance notice of the enforcement action. The airline said it was working with the Port of Seattle to determine whether established protocols had been followed and had raised concerns with the appropriate authorities.ICE has stepped up immigration arrests at airports since the summer, particularly targeting individuals it says have overstayed their visas.You use AI every day. articles.summary: The parties of caretaker Israeli PM Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks Sunday over whether to form a coalition govt, with
articles.body: The parties of caretaker Israeli PM Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks Sunday over whether to form a coalition govt, with Netanyahu's party insisting on keeping his main policies.Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud began their confab at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks last Sunday.Eisenkot has until Dec 6 to form a govt, with the possibility of a 14-day extension. His 48-member bloc needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority.Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity govt, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of Oct 7, 2023.But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot's refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. His ally Naftali Bennett, a former PM, also reiterated Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with "Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances".On Saturday, Yashar presented the resumption of talks as "a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible govt", saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity govt. Among other things, it demands an end to "all personal attacks and incitement to hatred" targeting the outgoing PM and his govt. It also called for bringing together "all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people", without the participation of Arab parties.On Friday, Eisenkot warned that he would not allow the talks to drag on, saying he was ready to submit to parliament \an "emergency national government". Although he did not spell out how, his statements suggest a two-stage plan: the swift formation of a minority govt based on the core opposition parties, and then broadening it.(This is an AFP story)You use AI every day. articles.body: In rural Mississippi, a mechanic who had spent much of his life getting by on modest means began an unusual personal transformation in 1975. Inspired by Glen Campbell's hit song Rhinestone Cowboy, Loy Bowlin adopted a new identity and began decorating his clothes with sequins. The transformation took years, turning an ordinary house into an elaborate display that extended from its rooms to parts of its exterior. Bowlin, who became known as the Rhinestone Cowboy, died in 1995. His work did not disappear with him, however. Several parts of the house, along with his distinctive clothing and furniture, were eventually transferred to a museum in Wisconsin, as reported by Kohler Foundation.Loy Bowlin's early life in rural Mississippi before the Rhinestone CowboyBorn in 1909 in Franklin County, Mississippi, Bowlin grew up in a rural setting where money was often scarce. He married Ina Mae Mitchell in 1933, and the couple farmed, while Bowlin also earned money by selling scrap metal. Their marriage ended in the 1950s. Following the separation, Bowlin experienced a difficult period, with depression becoming part of his life.His Christian faith offered him some comfort during those years. By the middle of the 1970s, he was looking for a way to change his circumstances and how he felt about himself.How Glen Campbell inspired the Rhinestone CowboyIn 1975, Bowlin began developing a new identity after being inspired by Glen Campbell's song Rhinestone Cowboy. The record, released in 1975, gave him the name around which he built his new appearance.Reportedly, he began decorating his outfits, turning ordinary suits and hats into brightly embellished pieces. Rhinestones, glitter and reflective materials became regular features of his clothing. His appearance gradually became part of a much larger undertaking, one that would eventually take over his home.Bowlin was no longer simply adding decorative details to a few personal belongings. He was creating an environment in which the same visual style appeared across his clothes, furniture and surroundings.A house transformed with glitter, photographs and found objectsThe house became the centre of Bowlin's artistic work. Over approximately five years, he covered its interior and sections of the outside with an assortment of decorative materials. There was little distinction between conventional craft supplies and everyday objects. Cut-out paper, painted designs, rhinestones, aluminium foil, tinsel, Christmas decorations and collaged images from magazines all became part of the composition.The surfaces were built up with bright colours and intricate arrangements. Photographs and magazine illustrations appeared alongside glittering decorations, while strands of tinsel and ornaments added another layer to the rooms. Rather than following a conventional approach to decorating a house, Bowlin treated its walls and furnishings as places where his ideas could take shape.The result was closely connected to the persona he had adopted after hearing Campbell's song. His clothes and home belonged to the same creative world, with the rhinestone-covered suits and decorated rooms reflecting one another.What happened to the house after Bowlin's deathBowlin died in 1995, but his decorated home remained on the property. Preserving it in its original location, however, was not possible. Houston-based artist and collector Katy Emde acquired the house after his death, with an important condition attached to the purchase: the structure had to be removed from the site.Emde documented the property before taking it apart. The process allowed the different components of Bowlin's creation to be recorded and retained rather than simply discarded. In 1998, Kohler Foundation, Inc. acquired the collection of dismantled materials.The foundation later gifted the preserved components to the John Michael Kohler Arts Center in Sheboygan, Wisconsin. The transfer included parts of the house as well as many of Bowlin's customised suits, hats and furniture.Preserving the work at a Wisconsin arts centreThe John Michael Kohler Arts Center became the home of material from Bowlin's unusual project. Its collection preserved elements of an environment that had originally been assembled in a private Mississippi residence, allowing the work to be retained beyond the lifespan of the building itself.The preservation also brought together different aspects of Bowlin's creative output. His clothing, furniture and architectural decorations were all part of the same undertaking, rather than separate collections of objects. Keeping these pieces together helped retain the connection between the man, the identity he created and the home he spent years transforming.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Chaar din ki chandani': BJP nominee removes village streetlights hours after losing Rajasthan panchayat polls
articles.summary: BHILWARA: In Rajasthan's Piplu Panchayat Samiti in Tonk district, poll results were followed not by slogans, sweets or silence - but by a vehicle that
articles.body: BHILWARA: In Rajasthan's Piplu Panchayat Samiti in Tonk district, poll results were followed not by slogans, sweets or silence - but by a vehicle that arrived to take away the streetlights.Around 50 road lights installed before Diwali in Ward No. 2 of Piplu Panchayat Samiti in Tonk district were removed Friday evening, hours after BJP candidate Priyanka Sharma lost the Panchayat Samiti election by 751 votes to rival Dhanna Lal of Congress. Priyanka is the wife of Alok Sharma, the personal assistant of Niwai BJP MLA Ramsahay Verma.Villagers said the lights were installed before the festival when Priyanka was in the fray. For once, they said, lanes and dhaanis (hamlets) that had long remained dark were lit up. The timing was not lost on them then. The timing of removal too is not lost on them now.When TOI contacted BJP MLA Ramsahay Verma, he sought to make light of the issue by asking who would foot the bill for the electricity consumed. "Prior to the polls, villagers demanded that the sarpanch candidates install lights. The candidates did so. The question was who would pay the electricity bill? We expected that the BJP sarpanch would be elected, but since a Congress sarpanch was elected, the lights were removed," Verma said.He added, "Locals are making this an issue only in order to defame me. My PA's wife contested the polls for the post of panchayat samiti member. The removal of lights is being raised unnecessarily. Allegations against me and my PA are baseless."Ward panch Kajod Prajapat alleged the lights were put up to woo voters and taken away after the result went against the candidate. "People did get relief from darkness, but this arrangement proved true to the saying 'chaar din ki chandani, phir andheri raat hai'," Prajapat said.According to villagers, a team from the electricity department arrived with a vehicle Friday evening and began removing the lights. When residents objected, they were told the lights were illegal.That explanation has angered villagers further. They asked why the department did not act when lights were being installed, and why action was taken only after the election result. They also questioned on whose instructions the removal was carried out, pointing out that similar lights exist in many other places.Assistant Engineer (AEN) of Piplu electricity corporation, Govardhan Chaudhary, said illegal lights would be removed. "In places where lights have been installed illegally, a department vehicle will be sent to remove them," he said.For Ward No. 2, the episode has turned into a bitter joke: the candidate lost, and so did the village's brief claim to streetlights.By: Somdutt TripathiYou Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger on meeting an increasing AI chips demand: ‘Our greatest innovations are still…’
articles.summary: Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has rejected the notion that chip scaling has reached a physical barrier, arguing that the accelerating needs of artificial
articles.body: Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has rejected the notion that chip scaling has reached a physical barrier, arguing that the accelerating needs of artificial intelligence (AI) require a huge 10,000x increase in computing efficiency, not just generational gains. Speaking during a fireside chat titled “Reality Check: Beyond Chips” alongside technology theorist George Gilder and Heritage Foundation director Bret Swanson at the COSM Technology Summit 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona, Gelsinger maintained that reviving Moore’s Law hinges on fundamental breakthroughs across five core engineering fronts.Following the summit, Gelsinger doubled down on his optimism on X, writing: “Is Moore’s Law dead? I say it’s time to wake it up!”Power bottlenecks threaten AI data center growthGelsinger warned that gradual chip improvements are no longer enough to keep up with modern AI and compute demands, especially as severe power infrastructure limits become a major bottleneck for innovation. Key pressure points straining the AI hardware rollout include sluggish grid growth as US energy capacity has grown only in the low single digits over the past decade, creating serious hurdles for hyperscale data centers – something that Elon Musk has repeatedly spoken about.Other things include long equipment wait times wherein new gas turbines face eight-year supply backlogs, while nuclear power projects take a decade to construct. Next-generation hardware is driving electricity needs sharply upward, with NVIDIA’s Kyber racks- featuring the GPU maker’s Blackwell NVL72 architecture, pushing power demands to a mammoth 600kW.Backing next-generation lithography, nuclear power and photonicsSince joining venture firm Playground Global as a general partner in March 2025, Gelsinger has actively invested in startups built to tackle these exact hardware and energy roadblocks. He has backed US government-supported lithography venture xLight, which is working to push past ASML’s 13.5nm extreme ultraviolet wavelength barrier. His portfolio includes nuclear capacity firm Alva Energy to help address data center power shortages.“Great to join industry leaders at COSM to discuss AI's demand for a 10,000x leap in efficiency. Incremental improvements won't get us there. We need breakthroughs across light, power, cooling, composition and packaging,” he added.Despite skepticism from industry watchers who argue traditional Moore’s Law scaling has run its course, Gelsinger insisted that semiconductor engineering is entering a new era of multi-disciplinary breakthroughs.“After 40+ years in semiconductors, I believe our greatest innovations are still ahead!” Gelsinger said.Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.body: Note: These daily predictions are based on your Vedic Moon sign (Chandra Rashi).Saturn continues its passage through Pisces, so the longer-term lesson across signs concerns boundaries, routine and what each person is genuinely able to carry. The Moon moves through Aries for the whole of this Monday, turning attention towards the self: energy, health, and how a person defines a position before answering anyone else. Chaturdashi adds a quieter note to the day. Read your sign for the practical responsibility that deserves attention, and judge it against what your own week actually looks like rather than against advice in general.Today's Shani Upay & CounselToday's Theme: An honest limit spoken once is worth more than hours of quiet overwork. Keep the day small, finish what you promised and check one figure instead of assuming it.Favourable Window: 11:46 - 12:28 (Abhijit Muhurta). Indian Standard Time, Delhi.Caution Window: 08:09 - 09:28 (Rahu Kaal). Indian Standard Time, Delhi.ARIESFocus: Pace, rest and spendingYour own energy sets the pace, so decide early what you will not do. With Saturn working quietly on rest and expenses, small leaks matter: a subscription you forgot, a favour that swallows an evening. If a work demand arrives, give a plain answer about capacity rather than a rushed yes. Simple health routines pay off today, and an early night is not a missed opportunity. Close one loose end before you begin a second thing.Action: Write down one task you will drop today and tell the person concerned.TAURUSFocus: Which commitments still matterA quiet day suits you better than a crowded one. With Saturn on long-term goals and networks, the useful question is which commitments still earn their place and which are just habit. If a group asks for money or hours, read the details before replying. Take stock of small expenses without announcing a budget to anyone. Rest counts as productive here. Write down two goals you actually want to keep and let the rest wait.Action: Review two standing commitments and cancel the one that no longer fits.GEMINIFocus: Reputation and completed workReputation and daily output are in focus, so let the work speak before you do. A senior's instruction deserves a careful written reply rather than a quick verbal one. If your network brings an opportunity today, ask what it costs in hours before agreeing. The pull will be to describe plans instead of finishing them. Pick one pending task, complete it, then send the update. Keep meetings short and your notes clear enough for someone else to follow.Action: Finish one pending task before replying to any new request.CANCERFocus: Ambition and trusted guidanceCareer pressure and guidance meet today. Saturn asks you to examine the beliefs you carry about ambition, especially any inherited from family expectation. If a mentor or senior offers advice, test it against your own judgment instead of accepting or rejecting it outright. On the work front, one public claim needs accuracy, so check a figure before you send it. Ask someone experienced a specific question rather than a broad one. The answer will be more useful that way.Action: Check one number before you send an official message today.LEOFocus: Shared money and trustWhat you share with others, including money, paperwork and trust, needs attention. Saturn asks you to be honest about what you do not control. If a joint account, insurance form or repayment is pending, read the terms rather than signing on trust. With the Moon highlighting belief and guidance, a conversation about values may drift into preaching, so listen instead. Admitting that you do not know something is stronger than pretending. Finish one document today.Action: Read the terms of one pending agreement before you sign it.VIRGOFocus: Clear terms in partnershipThis is a chandrashtama day, so keep the schedule light where you can and avoid drama. Saturn sits on partnerships, so an agreement with a spouse, business partner or colleague needs clear terms. If a conversation turns to who owes what, put the numbers on paper instead of relying on memory. Avoid final commitments on matters you feel uncertain about, and sleep on anything large. One small correction to a shared arrangement is enough for today.Action: Write down the terms of one shared arrangement and confirm it politely.LIBRAFocus: Daily duty and boundariesRoutine and health get the plain attention they need. Saturn wants discipline in daily work rather than grand plans. With the Moon on partnerships, an agreement about shared chores, time or money benefits from saying what you need without apology. If a colleague leans on you again, name the limit once, calmly. A short walk or an earlier bedtime counts as work on your health, not an indulgence. Choose the duty you have been avoiding and do it first.Action: Name one limit to a colleague and do the avoided duty first.SCORPIOFocus: Measured risk, steady routineCreativity, children, romance or a speculative choice needs a second look. Saturn asks whether a risk is measured or merely exciting. With the Moon on routine and health, the boring parts of the day carry real value: a checkup booked, an instalment paid on time, a task finished properly. If someone invites you into a quick scheme, ask for the numbers in writing. Keep the evening simple and limit your exposure on anything you cannot easily walk away from.Action: Ask for the numbers in writing before agreeing to any scheme.SAGITTARIUSFocus: Home matters, settled decisionsHome and your emotional base need attention. Saturn asks for steadiness rather than restlessness. If a household matter, repair or family arrangement has been pending, settle it today with a practical figure or a date. With the Moon on creativity and pleasure, enjoy something light without turning it into a plan. A conversation with a parent or flatmate may need one clear sentence rather than a long explanation. Small comforts at home restore more than you expect.Action: Fix a date for one pending household matter and confirm it.CAPRICORNFocus: Unsent messages and effortEffort and communication carry the day. Saturn rewards the message you have postponed, especially one that must be honest about a delay. With the Moon on home and family, a domestic matter may pull you away from work, so handle it directly rather than pretending it is not there. Speak plainly to a sibling, neighbour or colleague and avoid hinting. One courteous sentence settles more than an hour of explaining. Keep your promises small and specific.Action: Send the message you have postponed, plainly and without long explanations.AQUARIUSFocus: Pricing, speech and recordsMoney and speech need care. Saturn in this area asks you to state a price, fee or value plainly instead of undercharging to keep the peace. With the Moon on effort and communication, a short message or call will move something that has stalled for days. Read any bill or quotation before agreeing to it. If someone asks what you charge, give a real figure. Avoid discussing money in a rush or before an audience, and keep a record of what you promise.Action: State your fee or price clearly, in writing, before the day ends.PISCESFocus: Limits, health and routineSaturn in your sign asks you to be clear about what you are actually carrying. Health and identity are the practical focus, so look at sleep, daily routine and the commitments you accepted without thinking. With the Moon on money and values, an expense today may reveal what you truly prioritise. If a purchase is optional, wait. Say one honest sentence about your limits to a person who keeps asking. That is not selfishness, it is maintenance.Action: Tell one person what you cannot take on this week.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: IISc has Caltech-like culture of fundamental science
articles.summary: For Karthish Manthiram, a month at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in Bengaluru was less a visit to a leading Indian research institution than a
articles.body: For Karthish Manthiram, a month at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in Bengaluru was less a visit to a leading Indian research institution than a chance to become a student again.The California Institute of Technology professor and winner of the Infosys Prize 2025 in physical sciences spent his sabbatical at IISc’s molecular biophysics unit, working with professor Anand Srivastava’s group on a field quite different from his own. He chose the group after following its research on proteins and their ability to change shape.But what struck him most was not just the science. It was the culture around it. Manthiram says IISc has something increasingly rare in an era when universities are pushed to produce research that can be commercialised quickly: a willingness to spend years pursuing fundamental questions whose practical applications may not yet be clear.“I have rarely visited a place that shares the ethos of Caltech, where I am now,” he says. “Caltech has this love of science, this belief that fundamental inquiry is important.” He says the same culture is alive at IISc..That patience, he says, is not an indulgence. Major technologies often rest on decades of science that initially appears too uncertain, too difficult or too far from commercial use.Different way of looking at proteinsHis own research has largely focused on abiotic chemical transformations, using catalysts and materials to make useful chemicals without biological processes. But he had become increasingly interested in how nature itself performs chemical transformations. He had been following Srivastava’s work and, when he got the opportunity to spend a month in India, knew almost immediately whom he wanted to work with.The research concerned fold-switching proteins. The conventional assumption is that the amino-acid sequence of a protein determines a particular three-dimensional structure. Srivastava’s group has shown computationally that some proteins can adopt multiple structures instead.The group has developed Morpheus, a computational method for predicting multiple folds, and a newer version called Morpheus 3D. Manthiram says the work is at the forefront globally. If proteins can shift between different structural states, those states could help explain how biological systems behave and could ultimately open new possibilities for drug development. Manthiram points to proteins linked to circadian rhythms. “If you understand how that works, you then start to have the opportunity to think about what to do about sleep apnea, about narcolepsy,” he says.Excellent researchers & infraDuring his sabbatical, he worked in a computational group with access to state-of-the-art CPUs and GPUs. Modern computational biology increasingly depends on access to large amounts of computing power.He is equally excited about researchers in India. Those trained in Indian institutions who later join his group in Caltech, he says, are “exceptional”. They come with strong fundamentals and experience working on frontier problems. IISc, he says, is a “crown jewel” in global scientific recognition.Where he does want students to improve is in how they present their work. Scientists often become so immersed in technical language that they forget what it sounds like to someone outside their immediate field. Manthiram runs workshops at Caltech to teach researchers how to articulate their research vision in a short, clear form, and he held a similar workshop at IISc. He also teaches young researchers to build a professional presence online. His recent postdocs, he says, told him they had discovered his group through LinkedIn posts about research philosophy, papers or advice on graduate school. That means, to be noticed, researchers have to package their expertise so people can find and understand it.Communication also makes science move faster. When researchers clearly explain what they are doing, Manthiram says, colleagues can ask better questions, spot problems and suggest new directions.I had read Anand Srivastava's work. He's a faculty member in IISc’s molecular biophysics unit. And when I heard about the Infosys prize, it was apparent to me in a heartbeat as to who I wanted to work with and where I wanted to go. I would learn a lot in this setting, because it was very different from what I had done historically. But that's the magic of a sabbatical. You get to make yourself feel uncomfortable. My only request to Anand was one phrase, five words: ‘Treat me like a student.’Karthish Manthiram, Professor, California Institute of TechnologyFearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: Manoj returns to RG amid leadership tussle
articles.summary: Manoj Parab rejoins RG amid leadership tussle with MLA Viresh Borkar; factions dispute CEO records over party address and allege BJP-backed split attempt.
articles.body: Margao: Former RG president Manoj Parab returned to the party on Sunday, submitting his membership form to the central executive committee (CEC) after quitting in May 2026.Addressing supporters at a gharwapsi event at Porvorim, Parab launched a sustained attack on the party’s lone MLA, Viresh Borkar. Much of his speech focused on personal allegations against Borkar and his family, along with Parab’s rebuttal to accusations levelled by Borkar’s group. Parab offered little detail on a roadmap for a party gripped by an internal split, but pledged to “protect” RG, calling it his creation. “If I could form a party, I can rebuild it and get another MLA elected,” he said.As Parab returned, the Borkar-led faction alleged BJP was attempting to engineer a split for political gain, and claimed the office of the state chief electoral officer (CEO) was enabling it. The faction alleged Parab was using procedural loopholes, “aided by the bureaucracy”, to re-enter the organisation and later assert control.Central to the dispute is the postal address for RG on record with the CEO. Senior party functionary Aditya Dessai claimed the CEO’s office has three different party office addresses on record, and correspondence should therefore have been sent to all three. “Sending it only to the address claimed by the Parab-led faction smacks of bias. It’s clear Parab is backed by BJP,” Dessai alleged.Dessai also cited party records in other states. He said election notifications in Rajasthan and Chandigarh list Bicholim as RG’s official address, raising questions about why Goa’s CEO records have not been updated accordingly.The Borkar camp said it suspects a broader plan. According to a senior functionary, Parab will attempt to reclaim leadership and, if blocked through internal and legal routes, will seek administrative backing. “But we will not let that happen,” the functionary said.The address controversy has intensified over the past week. On Nov 17, Borkar served a legal notice on Goa CEO Sanjay Goel, accusing him of misusing his authority and deliberately sending official communication to an address other than the party’s registered office at Nagzerwado, Bicholim. Borkar cited an Election Commission of India (ECI) communication dated Nov 5 regarding the party’s 2025-26 contribution report, addressed to the Bicholim office.Borkar said the Bicholim address — H No 2385/A — is the party’s national office and is also mentioned in a March 24, 2024 Rajasthan gazette notification listing RG and its election symbol, football. In his Nov 17 notice, Borkar asked the CEO to update records and send all future communications to the Bicholim national office and the party’s new state office at Kamat Towers, Patto-Panaji, noting that the earlier state office at Gera Imperium Grand, Patto, is no longer in use. RG has also written to the ECI seeking a formal change of address.The Borkar faction conceded the leadership battle is damaging the party’s image and consuming time meant for organisation-building and election planning.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Goa | Silver Rate in Goa | Bank Holidays in Goa | Public Holidays in Goa | Petrol Price in GoaStay updated with the latest Goa news.
